summary: The Yenching Fellowship supports students of the Yenching Academy of Peking University, an English-taught, two-year interdisciplinary master's in China Studies in Beijing. It is open to international applicants, and to applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan on a separate track, for the September 2027 intake. About 120 new students enrol each year, roughly 75 percent of them international. The first-year fellowship pays for tuition, housing, a monthly stipend, one round-trip fare, medical insurance and research expenses; a second-year fellowship is available to those in good standing who stay in Beijing.
eligibility_notes:
Education: at least a bachelor's degree in any field, or current enrolment in a bachelor's programme with the diploma received by August of the enrolment year. Applicants with a master's degree are welcome; about 16 percent of past scholars already held one, and a graduate degree is not favoured in selection. Peking University does not allow enrolment in another degree programme at the same time. The 2025 instructions add that the bachelor's degree must be recognised in the Chinese system and that grade skipping or starting a degree mid-year does not count as receiving the degree.

Academic and personal record: an outstanding academic record, strong interest in interdisciplinary study of China, and a record of extracurricular achievement, community engagement, social responsibility and leadership potential. Prior China or Chinese-language study is not required, but candidates must show a study plan tied to their career goals. The 2025 instructions also ask for good mental and physical health, no criminal conviction, and willingness to follow Chinese law and university rules.

Citizenship: international applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport. Former mainland, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan residents who emigrated must show passport or citizenship documents dated before 30 April 2021 and proof that Chinese nationality was cancelled. Applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan apply on a separate track and also complete a supplementary application with Peking University graduate admissions. Mainland Chinese applicants must be undergraduates at a mainland university and apply through Peking University graduate admissions, not the international route.

Partner universities: students and alumni of partner universities must apply through their own university first, which does a preliminary evaluation and nominates candidates. Students of cooperating universities apply directly.

English: required unless your native language is English or you graduated from an English-taught degree programme (undergraduate or above). Accepted tests: IELTS Academic 7.0, TOEFL iBT 100, Cambridge English Scale (Advanced) 185, CET 6 at 600, or TEM 4 at a good level or above. Tests must be taken after 1 September 2025. Not accepted: TOEFL MyBest Scores, TOEFL iBT Home Edition, IELTS Indicator, IELTS Online, IELTS One Skill Retake. Scores must be sent directly by the test organisation to the Academy (TOEFL code C488). Applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan must submit a score even if they studied in English; without it they take English as a second language after enrolling. Mainland applicants must also submit a score.
age_experience_notes: There is no strict age limit. Apart from holders of the Zhuoyue Scholarship, no one over 29 has been admitted, and the average entering age is 23. Work experience is not addressed in the pages read.
funding_summary: All admitted students receive the Yenching Fellowship for the first academic year (12 months): tuition, accommodation in the Yenching Academy House, one round-trip travel stipend between the home base city and Beijing, basic medical insurance (the Academy reimburses the Comprehensive Insurance Plan for Foreign Students), a monthly stipend and research-related expenses including designated research trips. Students in good academic standing who stay in Beijing may apply for a second-year fellowship covering tuition, on-campus housing or an off-campus housing stipend, basic medical insurance and a monthly stipend. Second-year students who live on campus and work as student assistants can receive additional funding. The stipend amount is not stated.
programmes_note: One programme: the Master's in China Studies, two years, taught in English. Scholars choose one of six research areas, which sets the diploma title: Economics and Management (Master of Economics in China Studies), History and Archaeology (Master of History in China Studies), Philosophy and Religion (Master of Philosophy in China Studies), Politics and International Relations (Master of Law in China Studies), Law and Society (Master of Law in China Studies), Literature and Culture (Master of Literature in China Studies). The research area does not change course requirements. Required courses: Topics in China Studies Lecture Series, China in Transition, a weeklong Field Study Trip, Academic Writing and (for international scholars) a compulsory Chinese language course that can be waived with high proficiency. A thesis and oral defence are required. International and Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan students need at least 31 credits plus a passed thesis; mainland students need at least 34.
institutions_note: The programme is hosted by Yenching Academy at Peking University, Beijing. The Academy lists 74 partner universities, whose students and alumni go through their home university's preliminary evaluation first, and 45 cooperating universities, whose students apply directly. The first partner universities listed are Bogazici University, Duke Kunshan University, IDC Herzliya, Kyoto University, Middle East Technical University, NYU Abu Dhabi, NYU Shanghai, Sungkyunkwan University, University of Delhi, University of Hong Kong (Faculty of Arts), Vietnam National University, Waseda University, Yale-NUS College, KU Leuven, Leiden University, Lomonosov Moscow State University, LMU Munich, Sapienza University of Rome, Sciences Po Bordeaux, SOAS, St Petersburg University, Trinity College Cambridge, Trinity College Dublin, Ca' Foscari University of Venice, University of Milan, University of Naples L'Orientale, University College Dublin, UCL, University of Copenhagen, Durham University, University of Edinburgh, University of Turin, Arizona State University (Barrett Honors College), Columbia, Dartmouth, Georgetown, Harvard, Harvard Kennedy School, Indiana University Bloomington and Northwestern. The full list is on the Academy's partner page.

summary.detail: Two-year master's in China Studies, taught in English, at Yenching Academy of Peking University. Year 1: required credits and courses. Year 2: thesis and defence, with approval of the university's degree committee before the degree is conferred. Degrees are awarded in January and July. The academic year runs from early September to early July. First-year residence on campus is compulsory.

benefits.conditions: First year for all admitted students; second year for scholars in good academic standing who stay in Beijing.

benefits.limit_text: Accommodation in the Yenching Academy House in the first year
benefits.conditions: Year 2: on-campus housing or an off-campus housing stipend for those who stay in Beijing. Shaoyuan 6 dormitory; most scholars share a two-bedroom suite and bathroom with one roommate of the same gender.
Both years. Second-year students living on campus who serve as student assistants can receive additional funding.

benefits.limit_text: One round-trip fare between the base city and Beijing
benefits.conditions: The base city must be in the scholar's country of nationality; the Academy calculates the cost. First year only; the pages do not say whether year 2 includes a travel stipend.

benefits.limit_text: Basic medical insurance; the Academy reimburses the Comprehensive Insurance Plan for Foreign Students
benefits.conditions: Students must be insured for the whole study period and buy the plan by registration day; students without valid insurance cannot register.

benefits.limit_text: Research-related expenses, including designated research trips and the field study trip
benefits.conditions: First year. The pages do not say whether year 2 includes research funding.

requirements.text: Online application form submitted through the Academy's application portal. All materials in English unless noted.
requirements.conditional_rule: Students and alumni of partner universities must also go through their own university's pre-selection first

requirements.text: Personal statement of 750 words or fewer.
Statement of Research Interest of 1,500 words or fewer, excluding citations.
Curriculum vitae of at most two pages (limit stated in the 2025 instructions).

Diploma(s) or certificate(s) of enrolment. Documents not in English or Chinese need the original and a certified English translation. Offer holders later need a credential evaluation of the bachelor's degree (CSCSE for degrees outside mainland China, CHSI for mainland degrees).
Two academic recommendation letters in Chinese or English from full or associate professors (or equivalent) in your intended field of study.

English test report sent directly by the testing body to the Academy (TOEFL code C488). Accepted: IELTS Academic 7.0, TOEFL iBT 100, Cambridge English Scale (Advanced) 185, CET 6 at 600, TEM 4 at a good level or above; taken after 1 September 2025.
requirements.conditional_rule: Not required for native English speakers or graduates of an English-taught degree (Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan and mainland applicants must submit one)

requirements.text: Supplementary application on the Peking University graduate admissions system.
requirements.conditional_rule: Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan applicants only

application_steps.title: Check eligibility and your route
application_steps.detail: International and Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan applicants apply through the Academy's online portal from 1 September 2026. International applicants close on 30 November 2026 at 9:00 am Beijing time; Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan applicants close on 8 January 2027 at 12:00 noon Beijing time. Students of partner universities must first pass their own university's pre-selection.

application_steps.title: Take the English test and gather documents
application_steps.detail: Book an accepted English test taken after 1 September 2025 and have it sent directly to the Academy. Prepare the 750-word personal statement, the 1,500-word statement of research interest, CV, official transcripts, diploma or proof of enrolment, and arrange two academic recommendation letters.

application_steps.title: Submit the online application
application_steps.detail: Submit the form and documents through the portal before your deadline. Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan applicants also complete a supplementary application with Peking University graduate admissions. Reapplication is allowed; explain how you used the intervening year.

application_steps.title: Admissions Committee screening
application_steps.detail: The Admissions Committee screens applications on academic merit, leadership potential, international experience and long-term aspirations. Your personal statement should explain how you would benefit from the China Studies programme.

application_steps.title: Online interview for finalists
application_steps.detail: International and Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan finalists are interviewed in winter or early spring (international interviews are held online; Chinese candidates, including those from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, are interviewed in person at the university). Finalists are told about one week ahead.

application_steps.title: Decision and university approval
application_steps.detail: Decisions for international and Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan candidates come around April. Accepted candidates must complete internal university procedures and be pre-admitted, and an official acceptance letter is issued the summer before enrolment. The 2025 instructions say offers are mailed around the end of June after the Graduate School and the International Students Division approve.

application_steps.title: Visa, insurance and registration
application_steps.detail: Apply for a study visa at a Chinese embassy or consulate with the admission letter and the visa form (X1 for study over six months), then apply for a residence permit within 30 days of arrival. Buy the Comprehensive Insurance Plan for Foreign Students by registration day (the Academy reimburses it). Offer holders submit a credential evaluation of their bachelor's degree. Enrolment is in early September. Failing the enrolment qualification review means disqualification.

application_steps.title: Live on campus, complete the thesis and apply for year two
application_steps.detail: All scholars live on campus in year 1. A thesis and oral defence are required within two years; international students who have left Beijing may defend online with the advisor's permission. Students in good standing who stay in Beijing may apply for the second-year fellowship; international students may choose whether to stay in Beijing in year 2. The degree needs approval of the university's degree committee.

fetch_problems: None blocked. The detailed instruction page that was readable is for the 2025 intake and shows 2024 dates, so only its general rules (visa, insurance, credential evaluation, offer timing) were used.
notes: The current admissions page prints the TOEFL minimum as '5' (a 6-point-scale value); the 2025 instructions and the stored data say 100. The file uses 100 and editors should confirm on the portal.
Pages disagree on cut-off for former Chinese residents: current admissions page says before 30 April 2021, the 2025 instructions say before 30 April 2019. The current page was used.
Offer timing: the FAQ says decisions around April, while the 2025 instructions say offers are mailed around end of June. Both are given.
